title: The cost of going to a wedding
paragraphs: Weddings are expensive affairs – there’s nothing new or surprising in that statement. When we talk about the costs of a wedding, we often think about the financial toll on the person paying for it. The outlay on tiered cakes, the dress with a long train, appliques and veil, and canapes at the reception can all add up. But what about the guests? The cost to your friends and family to attend.

The first thing to think about when attending is the price of getting there. Even just a few hundred miles from where you live can bring some expenses – be it transport or staying in a hotel. But some people like to tie the knot in exotic locations, thinking it will make their special day even more special – on a beach in front of palm trees rather than somewhere closer to home. Going to far-flung corners of the Earth to watch the event can really be a dealbreaker for some when deciding if they can make it.

Then there is the gift. What do you give a person on their wedding day? In some cultures, asking for money isn’t the done thing. Sometimes the bride and groom may issue a list of items they want to receive that you have to pick from. But what do you buy? And if it’s money, how much do you give them? How much is too much? These are questions all attendees face – give too little and you may cause offence, too much and you may be out of pocket. And of course, you don’t want to be outdone by a friend giving more than you.

Finally, the last thing you want to feel when going to a wedding is regret about the amount you’ve spent. If you give a good gift and spend a lot on getting there, and the event isn’t great, or the food at the reception isn’t perfect, you might feel a little resentment. Therefore, only give what you can afford to give. Weddings can be expensive for everyone concerned. But people often overlook the cost for guests. In the end, though, that special day is supposed to be a celebration of love above anything else.

vocabulary.entry: toll /təʊl/ n. （金钱、时间等的）耗费
vocabulary.example: The war took a heavy toll on the country's economy.
vocabulary.translation: 这场战争使该国经济遭受了重创。

vocabulary.entry: outlay /ˈaʊtleɪ/ n. 开支；费用
vocabulary.example: There will be an initial outlay for equipment.
vocabulary.translation: 购置设备会有一笔初期开支。

vocabulary.entry: applique /əˈpliːkeɪ/ n. 贴花；缝花
vocabulary.example: The dress was decorated with floral applique.
vocabulary.translation: 这条裙子上装饰着花卉贴花。

vocabulary.entry: canape /ˈkænəpeɪ/ n. （正餐前的）开胃小食
vocabulary.example: We were served smoked salmon canapes at the party.
vocabulary.translation: 宴会上为我们提供了烟熏三文鱼开胃小食。

vocabulary.entry: tie the knot /taɪ ðə nɒt/ 结婚；喜结连理
vocabulary.example: They plan to tie the knot next summer.
vocabulary.translation: 他们计划明年夏天结婚。

vocabulary.entry: exotic /ɪɡˈzɒtɪk/ adj. 异国风情的；奇异的
vocabulary.example: She loves to travel to exotic destinations.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢去充满异域风情的地方旅行。

vocabulary.entry: far-flung /ˌfɑː ˈflʌŋ/ adj. 遥远的；偏远的
vocabulary.example: The company has offices in far-flung corners of the globe.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司在世界各地的偏远地区都设有办事处。

vocabulary.entry: dealbreaker /ˈdiːlbreɪkə(r)/ n. （决定交易、合作等能否成功的）关键阻碍因素
vocabulary.example: The high price was a dealbreaker for many buyers.
vocabulary.translation: 高昂的价格成了许多买家的拦路虎。

vocabulary.entry: the done thing /ðə dʌn θɪŋ/ 合乎礼仪的做法；常规
vocabulary.example: In this office, it's not the done thing to leave early.
vocabulary.translation: 在这间办公室，早退是不合规矩的。

vocabulary.entry: offence /əˈfens/ n. 冒犯；得罪
vocabulary.example: His words caused great offence to the audience.
vocabulary.translation: 他的话严重冒犯了听众。

vocabulary.entry: out of pocket /aʊt ɒv ˈpɒkɪt/ 手头拮据的；赔钱的
vocabulary.example: I was left a bit out of pocket after the holiday.
vocabulary.translation: 假期过后，我手头有点拮据。

vocabulary.entry: outdo /ˌaʊtˈduː/ v. 胜过；超越
vocabulary.example: She always tries to outdo her rivals in every competition.
vocabulary.translation: 她总是试图在每场比赛中战胜对手。

vocabulary.entry: resentment /rɪˈzentmənt/ n. 怨恨；不满
vocabulary.example: He felt a deep resentment towards his former employer.
vocabulary.translation: 他对前雇主怀有深深的怨恨。

vocabulary.entry: overlook /ˌəʊvəˈlʊk/ v. 忽略；忽视
vocabulary.example: We should not overlook the importance of mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 我们不应忽视心理健康的重要性。

vocabulary.entry: affair /əˈfeə(r)/ n. （重要或大型的）活动；事务
vocabulary.example: The wedding was a grand affair attended by hundreds of guests.
vocabulary.translation: 这场婚礼场面盛大，有数百名宾客出席。

vocabulary.entry: tiered /ˈtɪəd/ adj. 分层的；多层的
vocabulary.example: The cake has a tiered design with fresh flowers on top.
vocabulary.translation: 这个蛋糕是多层设计，顶部装饰着鲜花。

vocabulary.entry: veil /veɪl/ n. 面纱；头纱
vocabulary.example: She wore a white veil on her wedding day.
vocabulary.translation: 她结婚那天戴着白色的头纱。

vocabulary.entry: reception /rɪˈsepʃn/ n. 婚宴；招待会
vocabulary.example: The wedding reception will be held at a local hotel.
vocabulary.translation: 婚宴将在当地一家酒店举行。

vocabulary.entry: issue /ˈɪʃuː/ v. 发布；公布
vocabulary.example: The company issued a statement about the new product.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司发布了一份关于新产品的声明。

vocabulary.entry: attendee /əˌtenˈdiː/ n. 出席者；参与者
vocabulary.example: All attendees are required to register before the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 所有参会者都需在会议前登记。

vocabulary.entry: flung /flʌŋ/ adj. 遥远的
vocabulary.example: The explorer traveled to flung regions of the Amazon.
vocabulary.translation: 这位探险家前往了亚马逊流域的偏远地区。

vocabulary.entry: palm /pɑːm/ n. 棕榈树
vocabulary.example: Coconut palms line the beach.
vocabulary.translation: 海滩边种着一排排椰子树。

vocabulary.entry: celebration /ˌselɪˈbreɪʃn/ n. 庆典；庆祝活动
vocabulary.example: The city held a big celebration for the national day.
vocabulary.translation: 这座城市为国庆节举办了盛大的庆祝活动。

vocabulary.entry: concerned /kənˈsɜːnd/ adj. 相关的；有关的
vocabulary.example: All parties concerned should attend the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 所有相关方都应出席此次会议。

vocabulary.entry: regret /rɪˈɡret/ n. 懊悔；遗憾
vocabulary.example: She expressed regret for her mistake.
vocabulary.translation: 她对自己的错误表示懊悔。

sentences.english: Weddings are expensive affairs – there’s nothing new or surprising in that statement.
sentences.chinese: 举办婚礼是件开销不菲的事——这话一点也不新鲜。

sentences.english: When we talk about the costs of a wedding, we often think about the financial toll on the person paying for it.
sentences.chinese: 当我们谈论婚礼的花费时，往往会想到买单者要承受的经济压力。

sentences.english: The outlay on tiered cakes, the dress with a long train, appliques and veil, and canapes at the reception can all add up.
sentences.chinese: 多层蛋糕、拖尾带贴花的婚纱和面纱、婚宴上的开胃小食，这些开销加起来数目不小。

sentences.english: But what about the guests?
sentences.chinese: 但宾客们的开销呢？

sentences.english: The cost to your friends and family to attend.
sentences.chinese: 那些前来赴宴的亲友们要付出的成本，却常常被忽略。

sentences.english: The first thing to think about when attending is the price of getting there.
sentences.chinese: 出席婚礼，首先要考虑的就是往返路费。

sentences.english: Even just a few hundred miles from where you live can bring some expenses – be it transport or staying in a hotel.
sentences.chinese: 哪怕只是离家几百英里的距离，也会产生交通费、住宿费之类的开销。

sentences.english: But some people like to tie the knot in exotic locations, thinking it will make their special day even more special – on a beach in front of palm trees rather than somewhere closer to home.
sentences.chinese: 但有些人偏喜欢在充满异域风情的地方举办婚礼，他们觉得这样能让这个特殊的日子更难忘——比如在棕榈树环绕的海滩上，而非离家更近的地方。

sentences.english: Going to far-flung corners of the Earth to watch the event can really be a dealbreaker for some when deciding if they can make it.
sentences.chinese: 对有些人来说，要远赴天涯海角参加婚礼，会成为他们决定是否出席的关键阻碍因素。

sentences.english: Then there is the gift.
sentences.chinese: 接下来就是礼金和礼物的问题。

sentences.english: What do you give a person on their wedding day?
sentences.chinese: 婚礼当天，该给新人送点什么呢？

sentences.english: In some cultures, asking for money isn’t the done thing.
sentences.chinese: 在一些文化里，直接索要礼金是不合时宜的做法。

sentences.english: Sometimes the bride and groom may issue a list of items they want to receive that you have to pick from.
sentences.chinese: 有时新人会列出一份想要的礼物清单，让宾客从中挑选。

sentences.english: But what do you buy?
sentences.chinese: 可到底该买什么呢？

sentences.english: And if it’s money, how much do you give them?
sentences.chinese: 如果是送礼金，又该送多少？

sentences.english: How much is too much?
sentences.chinese: 多少算多哪？

sentences.english: These are questions all attendees face – give too little and you may cause offence, too much and you may be out of pocket.
sentences.chinese: 这些都是每位宾客都会面临的难题——送太少怕失礼，送太多又会让自己手头拮据。

sentences.english: And of course, you don’t want to be outdone by a friend giving more than you.
sentences.chinese: 而且，没人愿意在礼金数额上被朋友比下去。

sentences.english: Finally, the last thing you want to feel when going to a wedding is regret about the amount you’ve spent.
sentences.chinese: 最后，参加一场婚礼，最不想感受到的就是为自己花出去的钱而后悔。

sentences.english: If you give a good gift and spend a lot on getting there, and the event isn’t great, or the food at the reception isn’t perfect, you might feel a little resentment.
sentences.chinese: 如果你精心准备了贵重礼物，又花了不少钱奔波赴宴，结果婚礼办得不尽人意，或是婚宴的菜品难以下咽，心里难免会生出些许怨气。

sentences.english: Therefore, only give what you can afford to give.
sentences.chinese: 因此，一切都要量力而行。

sentences.english: Weddings can be expensive for everyone concerned. But people often overlook the cost for guests.
sentences.chinese: 婚礼对每个相关的人来说，都可能是一笔不小的开销，但人们常常忽略宾客的花费。

sentences.english: In the end, though, that special day is supposed to be a celebration of love above anything else.
sentences.chinese: 不过说到底，这个特殊的日子，终究是一场以爱为核心的庆典。
